6.9.3. Electronic Vaccine Intelligence Network (eVIN)

Maintaining vaccine potency requires strict adherence to the recommended storage temperatures throughout the vaccine supply chain. To strengthen vaccine logistics and ensure uninterrupted vaccine availability, Tamil Nadu implemented the Electronic Vaccine Intelligence Network (eVIN) in October 2019.

The eVIN platform enables real-time monitoring of vaccine stocks and storage temperatures, ensuring uninterrupted vaccine availability and maintenance of vaccine potency across all cold chain points in the State.

6.9.4. U-WIN Digital Immunization Platform

Incomplete vaccination, missed doses, migration of beneficiaries, poor record

345

maintenance and difficulties in tracking unvaccinated children remain major challenges to achieving universal immunization coverage. To address these challenges, Tamil Nadu successfully implemented the U-WIN Digital Immunization Platform during 2023–24.

The platform digitally tracks vaccination services for pregnant women and children up to 16 years of age under the Universal Immunization Programme. It facilitates beneficiary registration, vaccination tracking, QR-based digital certificates, SMS reminders and nationwide portability of immunization records.

Currently, 6,453 health facilities have been onboarded onto the U-WIN platform, strengthening programme monitoring and reducing the number of missed and zero-dose beneficiaries.

The Government of Tamil Nadu envisions an integrated Immunization Ecosystem in which eVIN, U-WIN, HMIS, ABDM, birth registration systems, and disease surveillance platforms are seamlessly connected. This integration will enable real-time demand forecasting, identification of missed beneficiaries and delivery of personalised immunization services.

346

6.9.5. Vaccine-Preventable Disease (VPD) Surveillance

Although immunization has significantly reduced the burden of vaccine-preventable diseases, these diseases continue to remain a public health concern due to the risk of outbreaks and disease resurgence. Therefore, a robust Vaccine-Preventable Disease (VPD) Surveillance System is essential to continuously monitor disease occurrence, facilitate the early detection of outbreaks, evaluate programme performance and support disease control, elimination and eradication initiatives.

Tamil Nadu maintains a comprehensive Vaccine-Preventable Disease Surveillance System with technical support from the World Health Organization (WHO). Surveillance is undertaken for Poliomyelitis, Measles, Rubella, Diphtheria, Pertussis, and Neonatal Tetanus to facilitate early outbreak detection, monitor programme performance and support disease elimination efforts.

6.9.6. Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) Surveillance

Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) Surveillance is a critical component of the

347

immunization programme that ensures vaccine safety and maintains public confidence in immunization services.

The World Health Organization (WHO) defines an Adverse Event Following Immunization (AEFI) as "any untoward medical occurrence which follows immunization and which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the usage of a vaccine."

Serious and severe AEFI cases are reported and monitored through the Government of India's Safe-Vac Portal, enabling timely investigation, causality assessment and appropriate corrective action.

Tamil Nadu has consistently demonstrated a strong commitment to maternal and child healthcare and has achieved remarkable progress in “Ensuring Healthy Mothers and Healthy Newborns” through sustained investments in public health infrastructure, skilled human resources, and comprehensive maternal and child welfare programmes.

The State has accorded high priority to maternal healthcare and has implemented several initiatives aimed at providing financial assistance to pregnant women, free delivery and newborn care services, emergency obstetric care, nutritional support, birth preparedness, and digital tracking of beneficiaries. These initiatives supported by a strong network of healthcare institutions and skilled healthcare personnel, have contributed significantly to improving maternal and neonatal health outcomes in the State.

3. Every year, the State records approximately 7.8 lakh deliveries, with institutional deliveries constituting 99.9% of all births as per NFHS-6. Among this, Government health facilities contribute nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries (53%) which reflect the central role of the public health system in providing maternal and newborn healthcare services. Among the Government institutional deliveries, 90% are conducted in 130 Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and New-born Care (CEmONC) centres.

4. The accessibility and affordability of these services offered at Government Institutions have strengthened financial protection for families and contributed significantly to improved maternal and neonatal health outcomes. This has been substantiated by National Sample Survey (NSSO 80" Round) which states that the average out-of-pocket expenditure per delivery in Government hospitals is only Rs.1,364/-, compared to Rs.63,473/- in private hospitals. Po

as the primary safeguard against major out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure and the high costs associated with diagnostics and referrals.

5. Recognizing the welfare and dignity of pregnant mothers and with a view to further strengthening confidence in public healthcare services, the Government of Tamil Nadu have decided to provide “one-gram Gold Ring” to newborns delivered in Government Institutions as a token of appreciation and remembrance, commemorating the birth of the child and celebrating the joy and significance of

motherhood through the Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam (Smitompedr srhies Gonr§lnb Hib).

6. As per the cultural idea of Thaimaaman Seer in Tamil Tradition, the Maternal Uncle (Thaimaaman) presents ceremonial gifts (seer) - customarily including Gold - to welcome the newborn and bless the family. Through this scheme, the Government assumes the role of the maaman for every child born in its institutions, presenting a Gold Ring as an enduring token of welcome.
